units.meaning: If an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee—including employees exempt from the FLSA's recordkeeping requirement, such as bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees defined in 29 CFR part 541—the employer bears the burden of proving that the employee has not worked the requisite hours.

In order to claim that full-time teachers (defined in 29 CFR 825.102) of an elementary or secondary school system, institution of higher education, or other educational establishment or institution (who often work outside the classroom or at home) are not eligible for FMLA leave, the employer must be able to clearly demonstrate that they did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months.
Cross-reference directing readers to 29 CFR 825.801(d) for special rules applicable to airline flight crew employees, containing no independent substantive requirement in this passage.

As an example under the rule placing the burden of proof on employers who do not maintain accurate hours records, an employer must be able to clearly demonstrate that full-time teachers (defined in § 825.102) of an elementary or secondary school system, institution of higher education, or other educational establishment or institution (who often work outside the classroom or at their homes) did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the teachers are not eligible for FMLA leave.
